title: Affine RHom of a pseudo-coherent complex is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], let $P$ be an object of $D(R)$ [def-pc-derived-category] represented by a bounded-above complex of finite projective $R$-modules, and let $L$ be an object of $D(R)$ represented by a complex whose cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. For chosen representatives, write $\widetilde P$ and $\widetilde L$ for the cochain complexes of associated $\mathcal O_U$-modules obtained by applying the module construction [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] termwise. Then $R\mathcal H om_U(\widetilde P,\widetilde L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] $\cong\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)}$, where the right side is formed termwise in the same way. Its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent and vanish in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clauses (1) and (3)(a), using Tags 08FT and 08G5

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above complex representing $P$ with finite projective terms, say zero above degree $b$. As in Stacks Tag 064U (proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)), choose finite projective $C^n$ with $F^{b}=P^{b}\oplus C^{b}$ finite free and inductively $F^{n-1}=P^{n-1}\oplus C^{n}\oplus C^{n-1}$ finite free for $n\le b$, with differential $F^{n-1}\to F^n$ equal to $d_P$ on $P^{n-1}$, the identity $C^n\to C^n$, and zero on $C^{n-1}$. The projection $E^\bullet:=F^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ is a map of complexes whose kernel is a direct sum of complexes $C^n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}C^n$, so it is a homotopy equivalence; $E^\bullet$ is a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules, zero above degree $b$. (A single principal open on which every term of $P$ is free need not exist when $P$ has infinitely many nonzero terms, so this global finite-free replacement is used instead of a localization.)

Choose a representative of $L$ bounded below, say zero below degree $a$, by applying the standard truncation construction in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] to a representative with cohomology zero below $a$. By [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom] applied to the bounded-above complex $E^\bullet$ of (finite free, hence) projective modules and this bounded-below $L$, the module Hom complex $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(E,L)$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)$, the isomorphism induced by the quasi-isomorphism $E\to P$ of Step 1. Here $C^n=\prod_{p}\operatorname{Hom}_R(E^p,L^{p+n})$ is a finite product over $a-n\le p\le b$, and $C^n=0$ for $n<a-b$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8, lemma-stalk-internal-hom, case (2), affine derived-Hom computation

proof.text: Applying the module construction [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] termwise is an additive functor, so it carries the homotopy equivalence $E\to P$ of Step 1 to a homotopy equivalence, in particular a quasi-isomorphism, $\widetilde E\to\widetilde P$; and $\widetilde{R^{\oplus r}}=\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, so $\widetilde E$ is a bounded-above complex of finite-rank free $\mathcal O_U$-modules, while $\widetilde L$ is bounded below. By [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model], $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal O_U}(\widetilde E,\widetilde L)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde P,\widetilde L)$ on all of $U$. Its degree-$n$ term is the finite product $\prod_{a-n\le p\le b}\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_p},\widetilde{L^{p+n}})=\prod_p(\widetilde{L^{p+n}})^{\oplus r_p}=\widetilde{C^n}$, and the matrix formulas for the differentials (matrices over $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$) show these identifications commute with the differentials. Hence $R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde P,\widetilde L)\cong\widetilde{C^\bullet}$, the termwise associated complex of a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)$.

Localization of $R$-modules is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so by the description of sections over principal opens in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], kernels, images and cohomology of $\widetilde{C^\bullet}$ are computed on every $D(f)$ by localizing those of $C^\bullet$; this gives canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal H^i(R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde P,\widetilde L))\cong\widetilde{H^i(C^\bullet)}$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clause (3)(a), localization of the affine Hom complex

proof.text: Each sheaf $\widetilde{H^i(C^\bullet)}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and it is zero for $i<a-b$ by Step 2. Combining this with Steps 3 and 4 proves the asserted isomorphism, quasi-coherence and vanishing in all sufficiently negative degrees.
